name: Pop Culture APIs
description: Practice data manipulation with fun, deeply nested datasets inspired by real API response shapes. Each theme features punny parody names and rich data structures that drill chained iterator methods, bracket notation, and complex transformations.
attribution: Original exercises with fictional parody datasets inspired by public API response shapes. All character names and data are humorous parodies for educational purposes.

exercises.title: Movies: Get All Titles
exercises.description: Extract all movie titles from the dataset using the map method.
exercises.instructions:
Write a function called `getAllTitles` that takes an array of movie objects and returns an array of their titles.

Each movie object has a `title` property (string).

Example:
```
getAllTitles(movies)
// Returns: ["The Shawshank Exemption", "The Codfather", ...]
```

exercises.title: Movies: Filter by Genre
exercises.description: Filter movies that belong to a specific genre.
exercises.instructions:
Write a function called `filterByGenre` that takes an array of movie objects and a genre string, and returns an array of movies whose `genres` array includes that genre.

Each movie has a `genres` property which is an array of strings.

Example:
```
filterByGenre(movies, "horror")
// Returns: [{ title: "The Silence of the Clams", ... }, { title: "The Whining", ... }]
```

exercises.title: Movies: Get Director Names
exercises.description: Extract director names from nested movie objects using dot notation.
exercises.instructions:
Write a function called `getDirectorNames` that takes an array of movie objects and returns an array of director name strings.

Each movie has a `director` property which is an object with a `name` property.

Example:
```
getDirectorNames(movies)
// Returns: ["Frank Darabonk", "Francis Ford Cappuccino", ...]
```

exercises.description: Filter movies released within a given year range.
exercises.instructions:
Write a function called `filterByYearRange` that takes an array of movie objects, a `startYear`, and an `endYear`, and returns movies released between those years (inclusive).

Example:
```
filterByYearRange(movies, 1990, 1994)
// Returns movies from 1990, 1991, 1993, and 1994
```

```
sortByYear(movies)

```

exercises.title: Movies: All Cast Members
exercises.description: Extract all unique cast member names from every movie.
exercises.instructions:
Write a function called `allCastMembers` that takes an array of movie objects and returns an array of unique cast member names across all movies.

Each movie has a `cast` array of objects, each with a `name` property. Some actors may appear in multiple movies.

Example:
```
allCastMembers(movies)
// Returns: ["Tim Bobbins", "Morgan Freebird", "Marlon Branflakes", ...]
```

exercises.title: Movies: Most Profitable
exercises.description: Find profitable movies and rank them by profit margin.
exercises.instructions:
Create a function called `mostProfitable` that takes an array of movie objects and returns an array of `{ title, profit, roi }` objects for movies where total revenue (domestic + international) exceeded the budget. Sort by `roi` (return on investment) in descending order.

- `profit` = (domestic + international) - budget
- `roi` = profit / budget, rounded to 1 decimal

Example:
```
mostProfitable(movies)
// Returns: [{ title: "The Codfather", profit: 238966411, roi: 39.8 }, ...]
```

exercises.title: Music: Get Artist Names
exercises.description: Extract all artist names from the dataset using the map method.
exercises.instructions:
Write a function called `getArtistNames` that takes an array of artist objects and returns an array of their names.

Each artist has a `name` property (string).

Example:
```
getArtistNames(artists)
// Returns: ["Bad Bunion", "Taylor Drift", ...]
```

exercises.description: Extract origin city and country from nested artist objects.
exercises.instructions:
Write a function called `getOrigins` that takes an array of artist objects and returns an array of strings in the format `"City, Country"`.

Each artist has an `origin` property which is an object with `city` and `country`.

Example:
```
getOrigins(artists)
// Returns: ["San Huan, Puerto Rico", "West Reeding, USA", ...]
```

exercises.title: Music: Artist Grammy Summary
exercises.description: Build summary objects with artist names and Grammy stats.
exercises.instructions:
Write a function called `grammySummary` that takes an array of artist objects and returns an array of objects with:
- `name`: the artist's name
- `wins`: their Grammy wins
- `nominations`: their Grammy nominations
- `winRate`: wins divided by nominations, rounded to 2 decimal places (or 0 if no nominations)

Example:
```
grammySummary(artists)
// Returns: [{ name: "Bad Bunion", wins: 3, nominations: 18, winRate: 0.17 }, ...]
```

exercises.title: Music: Albums for Artist
exercises.description: Find all albums belonging to a specific artist using cross-referencing.
exercises.instructions:
Write a function called `getArtistAlbums` that takes the `artists` array, the `albums` array, and an artist name string. It should find the artist by name, then return all albums whose `artistId` matches that artist's `id`.

Return an empty array if the artist is not found.

Example:
```
getArtistAlbums(artists, albums, "Billie Eyelash")
// Returns: [{ title: "HIT ME HARD AND GENTLY", ... }, { title: "When We All Fall Asleep...", ... }]
```

Write a function called `totalTracks` that takes an array of album objects and returns the total number of tracks across all albums.

Example:
```
totalTracks(albums) // Returns: 94
```


exercises.title: Music: Featured Artists
exercises.description: Extract all unique featured artist names from album tracks.
exercises.instructions:
Write a function called `getFeaturedArtists` that takes an array of album objects and returns an array of unique artist names that appear as features on any track.

Each track has a `features` array of artist name strings (may be empty).

Example:
```
getFeaturedArtists(albums)
// Returns: ["Quake", "Fuerza Refrita", "The Weeknight", ...]
```

exercises.title: Music: Artist Discography Report
exercises.description: Build a discography report for each artist by cross-referencing both datasets.
exercises.instructions:
Write a function called `discographyReport` that takes the `artists` and `albums` arrays and returns an array of objects, one per artist, with:
- `name`: artist name
- `albumCount`: number of albums
- `totalTracks`: total tracks across all their albums
- `totalSales`: sum of `certification.sales` across all their albums
- `topAlbum`: title of their album with the highest `ratings.fan` score

Sort the result by `totalSales` descending.

Example:
```
discographyReport(artists, albums)
// Returns: [{ name: "Bad Bunion", albumCount: 2, totalTracks: 11, totalSales: 11700000, topAlbum: "Un Verano Sin WiFi" }, ...]
```

hints: Process in two passes: first loop through artists to populate each label with its artist names, then loop through albums to add album counts and sales.
Use an object as an accumulator. For each label, track unique artists (check with .includes()), and count albums separately using album.label.

exercises.title: Music: Full Streaming Analysis
exercises.description: Build a comprehensive streaming platform analysis from both datasets.
exercises.instructions:
Create a function called `streamingAnalysis` that takes the `artists` and `albums` arrays and returns an object with:
- `totalArtists`: number of artists
- `totalAlbums`: number of albums
- `totalTracks`: total tracks across all albums
- `avgListeners`: average monthlyListeners across all artists (rounded to nearest integer)
- `mostGrammys`: `{ name, wins }` of the artist with the most Grammy wins
- `highestRated`: `{ title, artist, fan }` of the album with the highest fan rating (include the artist name by looking up artistId)
- `certificationCounts`: object mapping certification status to count of albums (e.g., `{ diamond: 4, platinum: 10, gold: 4 }`)

Example:
```
streamingAnalysis(artists, albums)
// Returns: { totalArtists: 10, totalAlbums: 18, ... }
```

Each game has a `title` property (string).

Example:
```
getGameTitles(games)
// Returns: ["Clair Absurd: Expedition 33⅓", "Balder's Gate 3", ...]
```

```
gamesSince(games, 2023)
// Returns games from 2023, 2024, and 2025
```

exercises.title: Video Games: Platforms for Game
exercises.description: Find all platform names a specific game is available on using cross-referencing.
exercises.instructions:
Write a function called `getGamePlatforms` that takes the `platforms` array, the `games` array, and a game title string. It should find the game by title, then return an array of platform name strings by matching the game's `platformIds` against platform `id` values.

Return an empty array if the game is not found.

Example:
```
getGamePlatforms(platforms, games, "Astro Botch")
// Returns: ["GameStation 5"]
```

exercises.title: Video Games: Unique Genres
exercises.description: Extract all unique genres from across all games.
exercises.instructions:
Write a function called `getUniqueGenres` that takes an array of game objects and returns a sorted array of all unique genre strings found across all games.

Each game has a `genres` array.

Example:
```
getUniqueGenres(games)
// Returns: ["action", "adventure", "battle-royale", ...]
```

exercises.title: Video Games: Sort by Playtime
exercises.description: Sort games by completionist playtime, excluding games without playtime data.
exercises.instructions:
Write a function called `sortByPlaytime` that takes an array of game objects and returns an array of objects with `title` and `completionist` properties, sorted from longest to shortest completionist playtime.

Exclude games where `playtime.completionist` is `null`.

Example:
```
sortByPlaytime(games)
// Returns: [{ title: "Mineshaft", completionist: 420 }, ...]
```

exercises.title: Video Games: Platform Library Report
exercises.description: Build a library report for each platform showing its games and player stats.
exercises.instructions:
Write a function called `platformReport` that takes the `platforms` and `games` arrays and returns an array of objects, one per platform, with:
- `name`: platform name
- `gameCount`: number of games available on that platform
- `totalPlayers`: sum of `players.total` across games on that platform
- `topGame`: title of the game on that platform with the highest `ratings.metacritic`
- `exclusiveCount`: number of games ONLY on that platform

Sort by `gameCount` descending.

Example:
```
platformReport(platforms, games)
// Returns: [{ name: "GameStation 5", gameCount: 10, ... }, ...]
```

exercises.title: Video Games: Full Gaming Analysis
exercises.description: Build a comprehensive gaming industry analysis from both datasets.
exercises.instructions:
Create a function called `gamingAnalysis` that takes the `platforms` and `games` arrays and returns an object with:
- `totalGames`: number of games
- `totalPlatforms`: number of platforms
- `totalPlayers`: sum of all `players.total`
- `avgMetacritic`: average Metacritic across all games (rounded to 1 decimal)
- `mostAwarded`: `{ title, totalAwards }` of the game with the most total awards (sum of gameAwards + bafta + diceAwards)
- `mostPopular`: `{ title, players }` of the game with highest `players.total`
- `manufacturerBreakdown`: object mapping each platform manufacturer to `{ platforms, totalGamesSold }` where `platforms` is an array of platform names and `totalGamesSold` is the sum of `unitsSold` (skip null values)

Example:
```
gamingAnalysis(platforms, games)
// Returns: { totalGames: 12, totalPlatforms: 6, ... }
```

Sort by `bst` descending.

Example:
```
getBaseTotals(pokemon)
// Returns: [{ name: "Ray-quiz-a", bst: 680 }, { name: "Mew-Two-Shoes", bst: 680 }, ...]
```

exercises.title: Pokemans: Type Advantages
exercises.description: Find what types a Pokemans is strong against using cross-referencing.
exercises.instructions:
Write a function called `getAdvantages` that takes the `types` array, the `pokemon` array, and a Pokemans name. Return a sorted array of all unique type names that the Pokemans's types are strong against.

Look up each of the Pokemans's types in the types dataset and collect their `strongAgainst` arrays.

Return an empty array if the Pokemans is not found.

Example:
```
getAdvantages(types, pokemon, "Peek-at-chu")
// Returns: ["flying", "water"] (electric is strong against water and flying)
```

Example:
```
canEvolve(pokemon)
// Returns: [{ name: "Bulb-is-sore", evolvesTo: "Ivy-sore", method: "Level 16" }, ...]
```

exercises.title: Pokemans: Average Stats by Type
exercises.description: Calculate average base stats for Pokemans of a given type.
exercises.instructions:
Write a function called `avgStatsByType` that takes the `pokemon` array and a type string, and returns an object with the average of each stat (`hp`, `attack`, `defense`, `spAttack`, `spDefense`, `speed`), all rounded to 1 decimal place.

Return `null` if no Pokemans match the type.

Example:
```
avgStatsByType(pokemon, "electric")
// Returns: { hp: 35, attack: 55, defense: 40, spAttack: 50, spDefense: 50, speed: 90 }
```

exercises.title: Pokemans: Type Coverage Report
exercises.description: Build a type coverage report for each Pokemans using both datasets.
exercises.instructions:
Write a function called `typeCoverage` that takes the `types` and `pokemon` arrays and returns an array of objects, one per Pokemans, with:
- `name`: Pokemans name
- `types`: the Pokemans's type names
- `strongAgainst`: sorted unique array of types this Pokemans is strong against (from its types' `strongAgainst`)
- `weakAgainst`: sorted unique array of types that resist this Pokemans's attacks (from its types' `weakAgainst`)
- `coverageScore`: number of types in strongAgainst minus number of types in weakAgainst

Sort by `coverageScore` descending.

Example:
```
typeCoverage(types, pokemon)
// Returns: [{ name: "Drag-on-ite", types: ["dragon", "fighting"], strongAgainst: [...], ... }, ...]
```

exercises.title: Pokemans: Generation Summary
exercises.description: Build a summary for each generation with stats and type distribution.
exercises.instructions:
Write a function called `generationSummary` that takes an array of Pokemans objects and returns an object where each key is a generation number and the value is:
- `count`: number of Pokemans in that generation
- `avgBST`: average base stat total (rounded to nearest integer)
- `types`: sorted array of unique types across all Pokemans in that generation
- `legendaryCount`: number of legendary Pokemans in that generation

Example:
```
generationSummary(pokemon)
// Returns: { 1: { count: 8, avgBST: 518, types: [...], legendaryCount: 1 }, ... }
```

exercises.title: Pokemans: Team Builder
exercises.description: Analyze a team of Pokemans for type coverage using both datasets.
exercises.instructions:
Write a function called `analyzeTeam` that takes the `types` array, the `pokemon` array, and an array of Pokemans names (the team). Return an object with:
- `members`: array of `{ name, types }` for each team member
- `totalBST`: sum of all team members' base stat totals
- `typesCovered`: sorted unique array of all types the team is strong against
- `weaknesses`: sorted unique array of all types that resist the team's attacks
- `uncoveredTypes`: sorted array of type names from the types dataset that do NOT appear in `typesCovered`

Example:
```
analyzeTeam(types, pokemon, ["Peek-at-chu", "Bulb-is-sore"])
// Returns: { members: [...], totalBST: 638, typesCovered: [...], ... }
```

exercises.title: Pokemans: Full Pokedex Analysis
exercises.description: Build a comprehensive Pokedex analysis from both datasets.
exercises.instructions:
Create a function called `pokedexAnalysis` that takes the `types` and `pokemon` arrays and returns an object with:
- `totalPokemon`: number of Pokemans
- `totalTypes`: number of types in the types dataset
- `legendaryCount`: number of legendary Pokemans
- `avgCatchRate`: average catch rate across all Pokemans (rounded to 1 decimal)
- `heaviest`: `{ name, weight }` of the heaviest Pokemans
- `tallest`: `{ name, height }` of the tallest Pokemans
- `typeDistribution`: object mapping each type name to the count of Pokemans that have that type

Example:
```
pokedexAnalysis(types, pokemon)
// Returns: { totalPokemon: 12, totalTypes: 9, ... }
```

Return an empty array if either character is not found.

```
sharedFilms(characters, "Luke Groundwalker", "Darth Tater")
// Returns: [4, 5, 6] (both appear in episodes 4, 5, and 6)
```

exercises.title: Star Wars: Faction Report
exercises.description: Build a comprehensive faction report using both datasets.
exercises.instructions:
Write a function called `factionReport` that takes the `planets` and `characters` arrays and returns an object where each key is a faction name and the value is:
- `members`: sorted array of character names in that faction
- `avgForceRating`: average forceRating (rounded to 1 decimal)
- `totalCredits`: sum of all credits
- `homeworlds`: sorted unique array of homeworld planet names

Example:
```
factionReport(planets, characters)
// Returns: { "Rebel Alliance": { members: [...], avgForceRating: 4.6, ... }, ... }
```

exercises.title: Star Wars: Planet Census
exercises.description: Build a census of each planet with its notable residents.
exercises.instructions:
Write a function called `planetCensus` that takes the `planets` and `characters` arrays and returns an array of objects (one per planet) with:
- `name`: planet name
- `climate`: planet climate
- `residents`: sorted array of character names from that planet
- `residentCount`: number of characters from that planet
- `avgForceRating`: average forceRating of residents (rounded to 1 decimal, or 0 if no residents)
- `totalCredits`: sum of credits of all residents

Sort by `residentCount` descending.

Example:
```
planetCensus(planets, characters)
// Returns: [{ name: "Croissant", climate: "temperate", residents: [...], ... }, ...]
```

exercises.title: Star Wars: Galaxy Database
exercises.description: Build a comprehensive galaxy database from both datasets.
exercises.instructions:
Create a function called `galaxyDatabase` that takes the `planets` and `characters` arrays and returns an object with:
- `totalCharacters`: number of characters
- `totalPlanets`: number of planets
- `jediCount`: number of Jedi characters
- `droidCount`: number of droids
- `wealthiest`: `{ name, credits }` of the richest character
- `mostFilms`: `{ name, count }` of the character appearing in the most films
- `speciesDistribution`: object mapping each species to its character count
- `factionSummary`: object mapping each faction to its member count

Example:
```
galaxyDatabase(planets, characters)
// Returns: { totalCharacters: 12, totalPlanets: 8, ... }
```

exercises.title: NBA: Team Report
exercises.description: Build a detailed report for every team using player data.
exercises.instructions:
Write a function called `buildTeamReport` that takes the `players` and `teams` arrays and returns an array of report objects (one per team) with:
- `name`: team name
- `roster`: sorted array of player names on the team
- `totalSalary`: sum of all player salaries
- `avgPPG`: average points per game across roster (rounded to 1 decimal), or `0` if no players
- `allStarCount`: number of All-Star players

Example:
```
buildTeamReport(players, teams)
// Returns: [{ name: "Los Angeles Fakers", roster: [...], totalSalary: 97440000, avgPPG: 25.3, allStarCount: 3 }, ...]
```

exercises.instructions:
Write a function called `buildSeasonSummary` that takes the `players`, `teams`, and `seasons` arrays. Return an array of summary objects (one per season) with:
- `year`: the season year string
- `mvp`: the MVP player's name (look up via `mvpId`)
- `champion`: the champion team's name (look up via `championId`)
- `bestRecord`: object with `team` (name), `wins`, `losses` for the team with the most wins
- `worstRecord`: object with `team` (name), `wins`, `losses` for the team with the fewest wins

Example:
```
buildSeasonSummary(players, teams, seasons)
// Returns: [{ year: "2023-24", mvp: "Luka Donuts", champion: "Boston Shelltics", bestRecord: {...}, worstRecord: {...} }, ...]
```

exercises.title: NBA: Conference Comparison
exercises.description: Compare Eastern and Western conferences by aggregating player data.
exercises.instructions:
Write a function called `conferenceComparison` that takes the `players` and `teams` arrays and returns an object with `Eastern` and `Western` keys. Each value should be:
- `teams`: number of teams in the conference
- `players`: number of players
- `totalSalary`: sum of all player salaries
- `avgPPG`: average ppg across all players (rounded to 1 decimal)
- `allStars`: number of All-Star players

Example:
```
conferenceComparison(players, teams)
// Returns: { Eastern: { teams: 5, players: 7, ... }, Western: { teams: 3, players: 5, ... } }
```

- `positionBreakdown`: object mapping each position to its player count (e.g., `{ PG: 3, SG: 2, ... }`)
- `dynastyTeam`: `{ name, championships }` of the team with the most championships

Example:
```
leagueDatabase(players, teams, seasons)
// Returns: { totalPlayers: 12, totalTeams: 8, ... }
```

- `type`: team type
- `status`: team status
- `members`: sorted array of hero names on the team
- `count`: number of members
- `avgPower`: average total power across members (rounded to 1 decimal), or `0` if no members

```
buildTeamReport(heroes, teams)
```

exercises.title: MCU: Full MCU Database

```
mcuDatabase(heroes, teams)
```

exercises.title: D&D: Get Character Classes
exercises.description: Extract each character's name and class.
exercises.instructions:
Write a function called `getCharacterClasses` that takes an array of character objects and returns an array of objects with `name` and `class` properties.

Example:
```
getCharacterClasses(characters)
// Returns: [{ name: "Randalf the Beige", class: "wizard" }, ...]
```
hints: Use .map() to build a new object from each character with name and class.
Return an object literal: `c => ({ name: c.name, class: c.class })`

exercises.title: D&D: Filter Living Characters
exercises.description: Filter to only characters that are still alive.
exercises.instructions:
Write a function called `getLivingCharacters` that takes an array of character objects and returns only those where `isAlive` is `true`.

Example:
```
getLivingCharacters(characters)
// Returns: [{ name: "Randalf the Beige", ... }, ...]
```
hints: Use .filter() to keep only characters where isAlive is true.
The boolean property works as the condition: `c => c.isAlive`

exercises.title: D&D: Get Spell Names
exercises.description: Extract all spell names from the spells dataset.
exercises.instructions:
Write a function called `getSpellNames` that takes an array of spell objects and returns an array of their `name` properties.

Example:
```
getSpellNames(spells)
// Returns: ["Furball", "Magic Missal", ...]
```
hints: Use .map() to transform each spell object into just the name property.
The callback is: `s => s.name`

exercises.title: D&D: Get Equipment Names
exercises.description: Extract all equipment names from the equipment dataset.
exercises.instructions:
Write a function called `getEquipmentNames` that takes an array of equipment objects and returns an array of their `name` properties.

Example:
```
getEquipmentNames(equipment)
// Returns: ["Verbal Sword", "Dagger of Venom-ous Reviews", ...]
```
hints: Use .map() to transform each equipment object into just the name property.
The callback is: `e => e.name`

exercises.title: D&D: Filter by Race
exercises.description: Filter characters by their race.
exercises.instructions:
Write a function called `filterByRace` that takes an array of character objects and a `race` string, and returns only characters of that race.

Example:
```
filterByRace(characters, "human")
// Returns all human characters
```
hints: Use .filter() with a strict equality check on the race property.
The condition: `c => c.race === race`

exercises.title: D&D: Highest Level Characters
exercises.description: Sort characters by level and return the top N.
exercises.instructions:
Write a function called `getHighestLevel` that takes the `characters` array and a number `n`, and returns the top `n` characters by `level` descending. Return an array of objects with `name`, `class`, and `level`.

Example:
```
getHighestLevel(characters, 3)
// Returns: [{ name: "Elm-in-stir Aumar", class: "sorcerer", level: 18 }, ...]
```
exercises.starterCode:
function getHighestLevel(characters, n) {
  
}
hints: Sort a copy of the array by level descending, then slice the first n entries and map to { name, class, level }.
Use spread to avoid mutating: `[...characters].sort((a, b) => b.level - a.level)`

exercises.description: Look up all spell names a character knows using cross-referencing.
exercises.instructions:
Write a function called `getSpellbook` that takes the `characters` array, `spells` array, and a `characterId` number. Return an object with:
- `character`: the character's name
- `spells`: sorted array of spell names the character knows (matched by `spellIds`)
- `count`: number of spells

Example:
```
getSpellbook(characters, spells, 1)
// Returns: { character: "Randalf the Beige", spells: ["Defect Magic", "Dish", ...], count: 6 }
```

}

exercises.instructions:
Write a function called `getInventory` that takes the `characters` array, `equipment` array, and a `characterId` number. Return an object with:
- `character`: the character's name
- `items`: sorted array of equipment names the character carries (matched by `equipmentIds`)
- `totalValue`: sum of all carried equipment values

Example:
```
getInventory(characters, equipment, 2)
// Returns: { character: "Drizzy Do'Urden", items: ["Bag of Folding", ...], totalValue: ... }
```

exercises.title: D&D: Spells by School
exercises.description: Filter and sort spells by their magical school.
exercises.instructions:
Write a function called `getSpellsBySchool` that takes the `spells` array and a `school` string (like `"evocation"` or `"abjuration"`). Return an array of matching spells sorted by level ascending, with objects containing `name`, `level`, and `damage` (empty string if none).

Example:
```
getSpellsBySchool(spells, "evocation")
// Returns: [{ name: "Eldritch Breakfast", level: 0, damage: "1d10 force" }, ...]
```
exercises.starterCode:
function getSpellsBySchool(spells, school) {
  
}
hints: Filter by school, sort by level ascending, then map to { name, level, damage }.
Chain: `.filter(s => s.school === school).sort((a, b) => a.level - b.level).map(...)`

Write a function called `getEquipmentByRarity` that takes the `equipment` array and a `rarity` string (like `"rare"` or `"legendary"`). Return an object with:
- `rarity`: the rarity string
- `items`: sorted array of item names matching that rarity
- `count`: number of items
- `totalValue`: sum of all matching item values

Example:
```
getEquipmentByRarity(equipment, "legendary")
// Returns: { rarity: "legendary", items: ["Cloak of In-Visibility", ...], count: 2, totalValue: ... }
```

exercises.title: D&D: Party Composition
exercises.description: Build a party by selecting characters of specific classes.
exercises.instructions:
Write a function called `buildParty` that takes the `characters` array and an array of `classNames` (like `["wizard", "fighter", "cleric"]`). Return an array of matching characters (whose class is in the classNames list), sorted by level descending, mapped to objects with `name`, `class`, `level`, and `hp`.

Example:
```
buildParty(characters, ["wizard", "fighter"])
// Returns: [{ name: "Randalf the Beige", class: "wizard", level: 15, hp: 78 }, ...]
```
exercises.starterCode:
function buildParty(characters, classNames) {
  
}
hints: Use .filter() with classNames.includes(c.class) to find matching characters, then sort and map.
Chain: `.filter(c => classNames.includes(c.class)).sort((a, b) => b.level - a.level).map(...)`

exercises.title: D&D: Shared Spells
exercises.description: Find spells that two characters both know.
exercises.instructions:
Write a function called `getSharedSpells` that takes the `characters` array, `spells` array, and two `characterId` numbers. Return a sorted array of spell names that both characters know (appear in both characters' `spellIds`).

Example:
```
getSharedSpells(characters, spells, 1, 6)
// Returns: ["Defect Magic", "Dish", ...]
```
exercises.starterCode:
function getSharedSpells(characters, spells, charId1, charId2) {
  
}
hints: Find both characters, then intersect their spellIds arrays using .filter() and .includes().
Get shared IDs first: `char1.spellIds.filter(id => char2.spellIds.includes(id))`, then look up names.

exercises.title: D&D: Total Party Gold
exercises.description: Calculate the total gold for a set of characters by class.
exercises.instructions:
Write a function called `getPartyGold` that takes the `characters` array and a `className` string. Return an object with:
- `class`: the class name
- `members`: sorted array of character names in that class
- `totalGold`: sum of all gold for characters of that class
- `avgGold`: average gold per character (rounded to nearest integer)

Example:
```
getPartyGold(characters, "warlock")
// Returns: { class: "warlock", members: ["Fjord Tough", "Tasha Yawn"], totalGold: 5880, avgGold: 2940 }
```
exercises.starterCode:
function getPartyGold(characters, className) {
  
}
hints: Filter characters by class, then use .reduce() to sum gold and calculate the average.
Average: `Math.round(totalGold / members.length)` — handle empty class with a ternary.

exercises.title: D&D: Character Sheet
exercises.description: Build a complete character sheet using all three datasets.
exercises.instructions:
Write a function called `buildCharacterSheet` that takes all three arrays (`characters`, `spells`, `equipment`) and a `characterId`. Return a detailed character sheet object with:
- `name`: character name
- `race`: character race
- `class`: character class
- `level`: character level
- `hp`: hit points
- `ac`: armor class
- `alignment`: alignment string
- `totalStats`: sum of all six ability scores
- `spells`: sorted array of spell names (from spellIds cross-reference)
- `equipment`: sorted array of equipment names (from equipmentIds cross-reference)
- `inventoryValue`: total gold value of carried equipment
- `netWorth`: gold + inventoryValue

Example:
```
buildCharacterSheet(characters, spells, equipment, 1)
// Returns: { name: "Randalf the Beige", ..., netWorth: ... }
```
hints: Find the character, cross-reference spells and equipment by their IDs, then assemble everything into one object.
Use Object.values(char.stats).reduce() for totalStats, and sum equipment values for inventoryValue.

exercises.title: D&D: Spell Popularity
exercises.description: Count how many characters know each spell and build a popularity report.
exercises.instructions:
Write a function called `getSpellPopularity` that takes the `characters` and `spells` arrays. Return an array of objects (one per spell) with:
- `name`: spell name
- `level`: spell level
- `school`: spell school
- `knownBy`: number of characters who know this spell
- `casters`: sorted array of character names who know this spell

Sort the result by `knownBy` descending, then by `name` ascending for ties.
hints: Map each spell to an object that counts characters whose spellIds includes that spell's id.
Sort by knownBy descending, with localeCompare on name as tiebreaker.

exercises.title: D&D: Class Summary Report
exercises.description: Build a comprehensive summary for each character class.
exercises.instructions:
Write a function called `buildClassReport` that takes all three arrays (`characters`, `spells`, `equipment`). Return an array of class report objects (one per unique class), sorted by class name ascending, each with:
- `class`: class name
- `members`: sorted array of character names in this class
- `count`: number of characters
- `avgLevel`: average level (rounded to 1 decimal)
- `totalHp`: sum of all hp in this class
- `uniqueSpells`: count of unique spells known across all class members
- `totalEquipmentValue`: total gold value of all equipment carried by class members
hints: Get unique classes with `[...new Set(characters.map(c => c.class))]`, then map each to a report object.
Use .flatMap() to collect all spellIds across class members, wrap in new Set() for unique count.

exercises.title: D&D: Full Campaign Database
exercises.description: Build a comprehensive campaign analysis using all three datasets.
exercises.instructions:
Write a function called `buildCampaignDatabase` that takes all three arrays (`characters`, `spells`, `equipment`). Return a comprehensive campaign analysis object with:
- `totalCharacters`: number of characters
- `livingCharacters`: number of alive characters
- `averageLevel`: average level across all characters (rounded to 1 decimal)
- `totalPartyGold`: sum of all character gold
- `richestCharacter`: name of character with most gold
- `mostSpells`: `{ name, count }` — character who knows the most spells
- `mostExpensive`: `{ name, value }` — the single most expensive equipment item
- `schoolBreakdown`: object mapping each spell school to count of spells in that school
- `rarityBreakdown`: object mapping each equipment rarity to count of items
- `totalCampaignValue`: sum of all character gold + all carried equipment value
hints: Break the problem into parts: character stats, spell school counts with .reduce(), equipment rarity counts, and cross-reference for total value.
Use .reduce() with an accumulator object for breakdowns: `spells.reduce((acc, s) => { acc[s.school] = (acc[s.school] || 0) + 1; return acc; }, {})`
